title: DigitalArchitectureFramework
description: JSON Schema of the DAF 7.0.0 Beta 6 metamodel, generated from technology/rdf/DAF-semantic-model.ttl. Relationships hold the ids of the related elements (x-reference names the target).

DAFBase.description: Synthetic common superclass for all DAF M3 classes. It carries the vendor-neutral properties previously represented by the OpenAPI DAFBase schema.

Created by.description: Identity of the user, system or agent that created the model element.

Identifier.description: Stable UUID identifier of a DAF model element.

Inspired by.description: The industry concept area a pack element is inspired by, for example process framework. It names an area, never an element of an industry standard. Empty for elements not supplied by a pack.

Modified by.description: Identity of the user, system or agent that most recently modified the model element.

Name.description: Human-readable name of a model element.

Pack.description: Key of the industry pack that supplies the model element, for example tel. Empty for elements authored in the model itself.

CapabilityBusinessValue.description: the value of a business capability

InitiativeStatus.description: a set of colors to Visually describe the health of the initiative.

ValueStreamCriticality.description: the criticality of a value stream

dApplicationStrategy.description: the disposition toward a certain application

dBaseStatus.description: Each daf object has a "Status" field

dConstraintType.description: Enumeration containing the various constraint types.

dCostFunction.description: Which line of the income statement an operating cost lands on.

dCostNature.description: Whether a cost is capital expenditure or operating expenditure.

dDepreciationMethod.description: How the cost of an asset is spread over its useful life.

dIncrement.description: The maturity of an entity, in order: None 0, Initial 1, UnderDevelopment 2, Defined 3, Managed 4, Measured 5. The initial value of each member is its order.

dLifecycleStatus.description: An enumeration of various Life Cycle Status .

dPricingBasis.description: What a contract price is charged for, read together with billableUnit and tariff.

dPrincipleType.description: An enumeration providing various principle types.

dProcessType.description: Enumeration for Process Type - Manual or Automated.

dRuleCertainty.description: How the rule entered the model.

dScala.description: a simple scala to assess status of properties

dAPI.description: OpenAPI Specification is an open-source format and initiative for designing and creating machine-readable interface files that are utilized in producing, describing, consuming, and visualizing RESTful APIs and web services.

basePath.description: The path, relative to the host, under which all operations are served. It starts with a slash, e.g. /v1. Use / when the API is served at the root of the host.

consumes.description: The MIME types every operation accepts by default, e.g. application/json. An operation can override it.

contact.description: Who to contact about the API: name, e-mail and URL.

definitions.description: The data types the operations send and receive, as a reference to the schema that defines them, e.g. the name of a dJSON_Schema.

Full Name.description: The full, human-readable name of the API, e.g. "Claims Intake API".

host.description: The host name or IP address that serves the API, optionally with a port, e.g. api.example.com:8443. No scheme and no path. Absent means the host that serves the documentation.

license.description: The licence the API is published under, as a name or URL, e.g. "Apache-2.0".

parameters.description: Parameters shared by several operations, defined once here and referenced by the operations.

produces.description: The MIME types every operation returns by default, e.g. application/json. An operation can override it.

responses.description: Responses shared by several operations, defined once here and referenced by the operations.

schemes.description: The transfer protocols the API supports (http, https, ws, wss). Absent means the scheme used to read the API description.

securityDefinitions.description: The security schemes the API uses, e.g. "OAuth2 authorization code", "API key in header X-Api-Key".

swagger.description: The OpenAPI (Swagger) specification version the API description follows, e.g. "2.0". Tools use it to read the rest of the description.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags that group the API's operations, e.g. "claims, policies".

dAPIAggregatesSchema.description: Aggregates Schema (Aggregates Schema). Ids of the dJSON_Schema elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dServiceRealizedByAPI.description: realized Physical Service (Service Realized By API). Ids of the dPhysicalService elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dAPIOperation.description: Defines operations exposed by an API for interaction with external systems. Also called endpoints.

base_Operation.description: The UML operation this API operation is generated from or extends, when the API is derived from a class model.

consumes.description: The MIME types this operation accepts, comma-separated, e.g. application/json. Empty means the API's default.

deprecated.description: true when the operation is deprecated and clients should stop using it; otherwise false.

description.description: A longer explanation of the operation's behaviour, rules and side effects.

hTTPMethod.description: The HTTP method of the operation, e.g. get to read, post to create, put or patch to change, delete to remove.

produces.description: The MIME types this operation returns, comma-separated, e.g. application/json. Empty means the API's default.

relativePath.description: The path of the operation relative to the API's basePath, with path parameters in braces, e.g. /claims/{claimId}.

schemes.description: The transfer protocols for this operation, e.g. https. Empty means the API's default.

summary.description: A one-line summary of what the operation does, e.g. "Register a new claim".

tags.description: Comma-separated tags that group this operation with others in documentation, e.g. "claims".

allowEmptyValue.description: true when a query or form parameter may be sent with an empty value; otherwise false.

base_Parameter.description: The UML parameter this API parameter is generated from or extends, when the API is derived from a class model.

collectionFormat.description: How an array parameter is serialised: csv, ssv, tsv, pipes or multi. Empty for parameters that are not arrays.

location.description: Where the parameter is passed: path, query, header, body or formData.

required.description: true when the client must send the parameter; otherwise false. Path parameters are always required.

dAPIResponse.description: Represents responses returned by API operations.

base_Parameter.description: The UML element this response is generated from or extends, when the API is derived from a class model.

default.description: true when this is the default response, used for any status code not described separately; otherwise false.

examples.description: Example payloads for the response, keyed by MIME type.

headers.description: The headers returned with the response, with their types, e.g. "Location: string".

Integer.description: The HTTP status code of the response, e.g. 200, 201, 404.

dActivityContainsAction_inverse.description: contains Action (Activity contains Action). Ids of the dActivity elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dActivity.description: Represents business or system activities. A function or work carried out by the business user.

dActivityContainsAction.description: is contained in Activity (Activity contains Action). Ids of the dAction elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUseCaseContainsActivities_inverse.description: part of UseCase (Use Case Contains Activities). Ids of the dBusinessUseCase elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dActor.description: Represents an entity (such as a person, system, or organization) that interacts with the system to achieve a specific goal. An actor typically performs actions within business Use cases and can be internal (e.g., employees) or external (e.g., customers or partner organizations), active and passive.

ActorGoal.description: What this actor wants to achieve when it deals with the organisation, in one or two sentences, e.g. "get a claim paid quickly".

ActorTasks.description: The main tasks this actor performs, in general terms, e.g. "files claims, uploads documents". Detailed behaviour belongs in use cases and processes.

ActorType.description: The kind of actor: a worker (internal or external) or a business partner (active or passive). Absent means not known; Not Set says the same and is kept for older models.

Count.description: How many parties act as this actor. Use unit {FTE} for staff and a party unit such as {customer} or {policy} for a customer segment. Absent means not counted.

dActorParticipatesInBizUseCase.description: Partecipates in Use Case (Actor Participates In Use Case). Ids of the dBusinessUseCase elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dContractServesActor_inverse.description: served by contract (Contract Serves Actor). Ids of the dContract elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleIsPerformedByActor.description: has Role (Role isPerformed By Actor). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationComponent.description:
An application component is a self-contained unit. As such, it is independently deployable, re-usable, and replaceable. An application component performs one or more application functions. It encapsulates its behavior and data, exposes services, and makes them available through interfaces. Cooperating application components are connected via application collaborations.

An application component may be assigned to one or more application functions. An application component has one or more application interfaces, which expose its functionality. Application interfaces of other application components may serve an application component. The name of an application component should preferably be a noun.

ApplicationType.description: The kind of application, e.g. COTS for a bought package, Custom for one built in-house, DB for a database.

BizCriticality.description: How critical the application is to the business, on a scale of 1 (can be switched off) to 100 (the business stops without it).

BizSatisfaction.description: How satisfied the business is with the application, on a scale of 1 (very unhappy) to 100 (fully satisfied).

Category.description: A free categorisation of the application, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Core insurance", "Back office".

depreciationMethod.description: How its Capex is spread over usefulLife: StraightLine or DecliningBalance. The depreciation schedule is derived from the Capex cost periods, inServiceDate, usefulLife and this method; it is not stored.

inServiceDate.description: The date the asset went into use; depreciation starts here. Absent means not recorded.

InvestmentStrategy.description: What you plan to do with the application: Retain, Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Rewrite or Retire.

ITSatisfaction.description: How satisfied IT is with the application, on a scale of 1 to 100. Low values usually signal technical debt.

LastStandardReviewDate.description: When the application was last reviewed against the architecture standards.

NextStandardReviewDate.description: When the application is next due for review against the architecture standards.

Owner.description: The person or team accountable for the application.

Port.description: The network port the application listens on, e.g. 8443, when it exposes one.

RetireDate.description: The date the application is, or is planned to be, switched off. When an initiative retires the application, use that initiative's finish date or later. Absent means no retirement is planned.

Source.description: Where the information about this application came from, e.g. a document, interview or tool export.

usefulLife.description: How long the asset is depreciated over, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P5Y. Absent means the asset is not capitalised or the life is not recorded.

dApplicationComponentHasContainer.description: Has Container (Application Has Container). Ids of the dContainer elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationComponentHasCostPeriod.description: has Cost Period (Application Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The application's run or change cost in one period, e.g. licences, hosting and support.

dApplicationComponentRealizesLogicalComp.description: Realizes Logical component (Realizes Component). Ids of the dLogicalAppComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationconfiguredbySystemConfigurat.description:
has configuration (Application configured by System Configuration). Ids of the dSystem elements; multiplicity 0..1. Relationship between dApplicationComponent  and
 dSystem

dApplicationConnectedWithApplication.description: connected From Application (Connects Application). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationConnectedWithApplication_inv.description: Connected to Application (Connects Application). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationExposesService.description: is exposed by Application (Application Exposes Ph. Service). Ids of the dPhysicalService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationHasOwner.description: owns Application (Application has Owner). Ids of the dStakeholder elements; multiplicity 0..*. Relationship between dApplicationComponent and dStakeholder

dApplicationRisk_inverse.description: has Risk (Application Risk). Ids of the dRisk elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationRunsInNode_inverse.description: is run By Node (Application is run By Node). Ids of the dDeploymentNode elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dInitiativeDeploysApplication_inverse.description: is deployed by Initiative (Initiative Deploys Application). Ids of the dInitiative elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dInitiativeRetiresApplication_inverse.description: is retired by Initiative (Initiative Retires Application). Ids of the dInitiative elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleMaintainsApplication_inverse.description: is maintained by Role (Role Maintains Application). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dTest_ApplicationComponent_inverse.description: is validated by test (Test validates Component). Ids of the dTest elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dApplicationAggregatesFunction_inverse.description: part of Application (aggregates Function). Ids of the dLogicalAppComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dControllerImplementsFunction_inverse.description: has Controller (controller Implements function). Ids of the dController elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dBusinessArea.description: an organization of Business interests, can be decomposed.

dBusinessAreaHasCapability.description: has Capability (has Capability). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 1..*.

dBusinessProcess.description: A sequence of activities that produce a specific service or product supporting a particular business capability

Category.description: A free categorisation of the process, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Core", "Support", "Management".

isAdopted.description: true when the people who should follow the process actually do; otherwise false.

isDocumented.description: true when the process is written down (procedure, model or work instruction); otherwise false.

isEffective.description: true when the process delivers its expected outcome; otherwise false.

isOptimized.description: true when the process has been improved for cost and speed and has no known waste; otherwise false.

LastStandardReviewDate.description: When the process was last reviewed.

NextStandardReviewDate.description: When the process is next due for review.

Owner.description: The person or role accountable for the process.

ProcessCriticality.description: How critical the process is to business operations: High, Medium or Low. Absent means not assessed; unknown says the same and is kept for older models.

ProcessType.description: How the process is carried out: Manual, Automatic (by IT) or Client facing.

ProcessVolumetrics.description: How often the process runs, as a count per period, e.g. 120 {claim} per P1D. Absent means not measured.

RetireDate.description: The date the process stops, or is planned to stop, being used. Absent means no retirement is planned.

Source.description: Where the information about this process came from, e.g. a document, interview or tool export.

StandardCreationDate.description: The date the process was first defined or adopted as a standard.

dEventTriggersProcess_inverse.description: is triggered by Event (Event Triggers Process). Ids of the dEvent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dInitiativeChangesProcess_inverse.description: is changed by Initiative (Initiative Changes Process). Ids of the dInitiative elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessControlsProcess.description: controls Process (Process Controls Process). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*. The source process checks or constrains the target; when it fails, the target produces worse outcomes. Not a sequence flow.

dProcessControlsProcess_inverse.description: is controlled by Process (Process Controls Process). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessEnsureCorrectOperationOfCapabili.description: Ensure the correct  Operation of Capability (Ensure the correct Operation of). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessFlowsToProcess.description: Sequence Flow To (Process Flows to Process). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessFlowsToProcess_inverse.description: Sequence Flow From (Process Flows to Process). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessOrchestratesService.description: Has Service (Process Orchestrates Service). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessResultsInEvent.description: results in Event (Process Results in Event). Ids of the dEvent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProductIncludesProcess_inverse.description: Is part of Product (Product Includes Process). Ids of the dProduct elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dValueStreamIncludesProcesses_inverse.description: is part of Value Stream (Value Stream Includes Processes). Ids of the dValueStream elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dBusinessService.description:
1. A repeatable activity; a discrete behavior that a building block may be requested or otherwise triggered to perform.
  2. A service provided by Business that achieve a business outcome in response to a request.

Category.description: A free categorisation of the service, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Customer service", "Internal".

LastStandardReviewDate.description: When the service was last reviewed.

NextStandardReviewDate.description: When the service is next due for review.

Owner.description: The person or role accountable for the service.

RetireDate.description: The date the service stops, or is planned to stop, being offered. Absent means no retirement is planned.

Source.description: Where the information about this service came from, e.g. a document, interview or tool export.

dBizServIsDescribedByUseCase_inverse.description: described by Use Case (Biz Serv Is Described By Use Case). Ids of the dBusinessUseCase elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dBizServUsesDataEntity.description: uses Data (Service Uses Data). Ids of the dDataEntity elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dLogAppCompExposesBizService_inverse.description: service run by application (exposes Biz Service). Ids of the dLogicalAppComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dPhysicalServiceImplementsBusinessServic.description: is Implemented by physical service (Physical Serv. Implements Biz Serv.). Ids of the dPhysicalService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessOrchestratesService_inverse.description: part of Process (Process Orchestrates Service). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRelatedService.description: Target Service (Child Process). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRelatedService_inverse.description: Source Service (Child Process). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleConsumesService_inverse.description: is consumed by Role (Role Consumes Service). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleStaffsService_inverse.description: is staffed by Role (Role Staffs Service). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dBusinessUseCase.description: Encapsulates business processes producing value for an enterprise.

Extensions.description: Alternative and error paths, each referring to the step of the main scenario where it branches, e.g. "3a. Policy has lapsed: ...".

GoalInContext.description: The goal of the primary actor, written as a short verb phrase, e.g. "Enrol student in seminar".

isCore.description: true when the use case is part of the core of the system and must be delivered first; otherwise false.

Level.description: The level of detail of the use case, e.g. summary, user goal or sub-function.

MainSuccessScenario.description: The numbered steps of the normal path through the use case, when everything goes as expected (the "happy path").

OtherActors.description: The secondary actors that take part in the use case, besides the primary actor. Repeats what the diagram shows, so the use case can be read on its own.

Precondition.description: What must be true before the use case can start, e.g. "the customer is logged in" or another use case that must have completed.

Scope.description: The system or business area the use case describes, e.g. "Claims portal".

Trigger.description: The event that starts the use case, e.g. "customer reports a car accident".

dActorParticipatesInBizUseCase_inverse.description: is executed by Actor (Actor Participates In Use Case). Ids of the dActor elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dBizServIsDescribedByUseCase.description: Has service (Biz Serv Is Described By Use Case). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dFeatureIsRealizedByUseCase.description: realizes Feature (Feature is realized by Use Case). Ids of the dFeature elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUseCaseContainsActivities.description: has Activitiy (Use Case Contains Activities). Ids of the dActivity elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUseCaseHasStory_inverse.description: Can be told as User Story (Use Case Has Story). Ids of the dUserStory elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUseCaseisImplementedByController_invers.description: Is implemented by Controller (Use Case is Implemented By Controller). Ids of the dController elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dCapability.description: Represents an organizational capability to achieve business outcomes.Can be current available in an Organization Unit (or) A business-focused outcome that is delivered by the completion of one or more work packages (by increasing the capability Maturity).

BusinessValue.description: How much value the capability brings to the enterprise: Low, Medium or High, or Support (needed but not distinctive) or Differentiator (sets you apart from competitors).

Category.description: A free categorisation of the capability, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Customer management".

CostScope.description: Deprecated: dCapability.Cost is removed. A capability's own cost periods (dCapabilityHasCostPeriod) hold only direct cost, and its full cost is derived from the cost periods of its linked roles and applications. Ignored by tools; do not set.

Criticality.description: How critical the capability is, measured by the cost of it failing, on a scale of 1 (minor) to 100 (the business cannot operate).

HierarchyLevel.description: The level of this capability in the capability map: 1 for top-level capabilities, 2 for their children, and so on. It is not the maturity: use Increments for that.

Increments.description: The current (as-is) maturity of the capability, from None (0) to Measured (5). Absent means not assessed, which is not the same as None.

IncrementsToBe.description: The maturity the capability should reach (to-be), from None (0) to Measured (5). Initiatives that raise it are linked by dInitiativeIncreasesMaturityOf. Absent means no target set.

IncrementSupplyChain.description: The maturity of this capability among your partners and suppliers, from None (0) to Measured (5). Absent means not assessed.

IncrementVertical.description: The typical maturity of this capability in your industry, from None (0) to Measured (5), for benchmarking. Absent means not assessed.

Owner.description: The person or role accountable for the capability.

Risk.description: How much risk is attached to the capability, on a scale of 1 (low) to 100 (very high).

Source.description: Where the information about this capability came from, e.g. a document, interview or tool export.

dBusinessAreaHasCapability_inverse.description: is organized in Biz Area (has Capability). Ids of the dBusinessArea elements; multiplicity 1.

dCapabilityHasCostPeriod.description: has Cost Period (Capability Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The direct cost of the capability in one period: cost no linked role or application carries. Its full cost is derived by adding the cost periods of its linked roles and applications.

dCapabilityisMeasuredByKPI.description: is Measured By Indicator (is Measured By KPI). Ids of the dMeasurementIndicator elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dDataEntityInformsCapability.description: is informed by Data Entity (informs Capability). Ids of the dDataEntity elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dGoalisOperationalizedByCapability.description: support Goal (goal is Operationalized By Capability). Ids of the dGoal elements; multiplicity 1..*.

dInitiativeIncreasesMaturityOf_inverse.description: is matured by Initiative (Initiative Increases Maturity Of Capability). Ids of the dInitiative elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dLogicalApplicationComponentSupportsCapa.description: supported by Application (App Supports Capability). Ids of the dLogicalAppComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProcessEnsureCorrectOperationOfCapabili.description: is operated by Process (Ensure the correct Operation of). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dResourceSupportsCapability_inverse.description: is supported By Resource (Resource supports Capability). Ids of the dResource elements; multiplicity 1..*.

dRoleExecutesCapability.description: is executed by Role (role Executes Capability). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dValueStreamEnablesCapability_inverse.description: is Enabled by Value Stream (Value Stream Enables Capability). Ids of the dValueStream elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dCluster.description: Represents a set of nodes working in the same Region, akin to ArchiMate’s Node concept within a server infrastructure.

dClusterContainsDeploymentNode.description: Contains DeploymentNode (Cluster Contains Node). Ids of the dDeploymentNode elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dDeploymentModelAggregatesCluster_invers.description: is Aggregated in Deployment Model (Deployment Model Aggregates Cluster). Ids of the dDeploymentModel elements; multiplicity 1.

dRegionAggregatesCluster_inverse.description: is Aggregated in Region (Region Aggregates Cluster). Ids of the dRegion elements; multiplicity 1.

dContainer.description: Encapsulates application components and services, mirroring ArchiMate's concept of a Node, where an application runs.

dApplicationComponentHasContainer_invers.description: contains Application (Application Has Container). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dContainerAggregatesVolume.description: Aggregates Volume (Container Aggregates Volume). Ids of the dVolume elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dContract.description: Provides an agreement between a service consumer and a service provider that establishes functional and non-functional parameters for interaction.

AvailabilityCharacteristics.description: The availability the provider must deliver, e.g. "99.9 % per month".

billableUnit.description: The unit that is billed, as a UCUM code: a usage unit such as {transaction} or GBy for PerUnit, or a party such as {policy} or {subscriber} for PerPartyPerPeriod.

ConsumingService.description: The name of the service that uses this contract. Prefer the contract's relationships when the service is in the model.

Description.description: A short description of what the contract covers. When pricingBasis is Other, explain the pricing here.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the contract applies. Absent means it applies from before the model's time frame.

effectiveTo.description: The last day the contract applies; after effectiveFrom. Absent means open-ended.

Growth.description: The expected growth of demand under the contract, e.g. "+5 % per year".

Owner.description: The role accountable for the contract.

pricingBasis.description: What the price is charged for. Read it together with billableUnit and tariff: PerUnit (tariff x units used), PerPartyPerPeriod (tariff per party per tariff.per), FlatFee (tariff per tariff.per), Tiered (volume bands, not modelled) or Other (explained in Description). Absent means not priced.

ProvidingService.description: The name of the service that provides this contract. Prefer the contract's relationships when the service is in the model.

renewal.description: How often the contract renews, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P1Y. Absent means it does not renew automatically.

ResponseRequirements.description: The response times the provider must meet, e.g. "95 % of requests within 2 s".

ServiceTimes.description: When the service must be available, e.g. "Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 ET" or "24x7".

Source.description: Where the information about this contract came from, e.g. the signed agreement.

tariff.description: The price components, each a quantity with its own basis, e.g. 105 CAD per P1M basis "per unit" and 1 CAD per P1M basis "per door". Their sum is the price. Read together with pricingBasis and billableUnit.

Throughput.description: The capacity the provider must support, e.g. "500 requests per second".

ContractRelatedProduct.description: relates to Product (Contract is Related to Product). Ids of the dProduct elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dContractHasRevenuePeriod.description: has Revenue Period (Contract Has Revenue Period). Ids of the dRevenuePeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The recurring revenue billed under the contract in one period, e.g. a service subscription.

dContractServesActor.description: is serving actor (Contract Serves Actor). Ids of the dActor elements; multiplicity 0..*. a contract is serving a actor of type Partner

dController.description: Encapsulates application behavior and flow logic.

dActionKey.description: target Controller (Action Key). Ids of the dController elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dActionKey_inverse.description: Source Controller (Action Key). Ids of the dController elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dControllerControlsModel.description: Controls Model (Controls Model). Ids of the dModelClass elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dControllerGovernsView.description: Governs view (Governs View). Ids of the dView elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dControllerImplementsFunction.description: Implements function (controller Implements function). Ids of the dApplicationFunction elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dObjectInstanceofController_inverse.description: Istance of Controller (Instance of Controller). Ids of the dObject elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUseCaseisImplementedByController.description: implements Use Case (Use Case is Implemented By Controller). Ids of the dBusinessUseCase elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dCostPeriod.description: Spend, or a spending cap, of one element in one period, planned or actual. Spend belongs to an initiative, application, role, capability, product or resource; a cap belongs to a program (its budget). costNature says whether it is capital or operating spend, and costFunction which line of the income statement an operating cost lands on. Spend can be included in the financial period of the organisation unit whose books it lands in (dFinancialPeriodIncludesCostPeriod).

amount.description: The money spent, or allowed, in the period, with an ISO 4217 currency as unit. Use kind Actual for spend that happened and Estimate for a plan.

costFunction.description: For an operating cost, the line of the income statement it lands on: CostOfRevenue, SellingGeneralAdmin or ResearchDevelopment. Not set for Capex, which is not an income-statement cost. Absent means not classified.

costNature.description: Whether the amount is capital (Capex) or operating (Opex) expenditure. Absent means the amount covers both, as a budget cap does.

periodLength.description: The length of the period, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P1M, P3M, P1Y. The cost periods of one owner must not overlap.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period.

dApplicationComponentHasCostPeriod_inver.description: is cost of Application (Application Has Cost Period). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dCapabilityHasCostPeriod_inverse.description: is direct cost of Capability (Capability Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dFinancialPeriodIncludesCostPeriod_inver.description: is included in Financial Period (Financial Period Includes Cost Period). Ids of the dFinancialPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dInitiativeHasCostPeriod_inverse.description: is cost of Initiative (Initiative Has Cost Period). Ids of the dInitiative elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dProductHasCostPeriod_inverse.description: is cost of Product (Product Has Cost Period). Ids of the dProduct elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dProgramHasBudgetPeriod_inverse.description: is budget of Program (Program Has Budget Period). Ids of the dProgram elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dResourceHasCostPeriod_inverse.description: is cost of Resource (Resource Has Cost Period). Ids of the dResource elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dRoleHasCostPeriod_inverse.description: is cost of Role (Role Has Cost Period). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..1.

isAccurate.description: true when the data correctly represents the real-world thing it describes; otherwise false.

isTimely.description: true when the data is up to date when it is used; otherwise false.

PrivacyClassification.description: How restricted access to the data is, following your classification scheme, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Personal.

RelatedDecisions.description: Other decisions this one depends on, replaces or affects.

dEvent.description: Something that happens, inside or outside the organization, that triggers behaviour or results from it.

duration.description: How long the event lasts, as an xsd:duration, e.g. PT4H. Use it when the dates are not known.

endDate.description: When the event, or the window of a possible event, ends; after startDate. Absent means it has not ended or is instantaneous.

eventType.description: Where the event comes from: Business (a business fact), Temporal (a point in time, e.g. month end), External (outside the organisation) or Technical (a system event). Absent means not classified.

frequency.description: How often a recurring event happens, as a count per period, e.g. 120 {claim} per P1D. Set only when nature is Recurring.

likelihood.description: How likely a possible event is, on a scale of 1 (very unlikely) to 100 (almost certain), as for dRisk.likelihood. Set only when nature is Possible.

nature.description: Recurring: a designed trigger that happens regularly (set frequency). Possible: an event in a scenario that may happen (set likelihood). Occurred: an event that has happened (set startDate).

owner.description: The role accountable for responding to the event.

Source.description: Where the information about this event came from, e.g. an incident record or a scenario workshop.

startDate.description: When an occurred event started, or when the window of a possible event opens.

dEventLeadsToEvent_inverse.description: follows Event (Event Leads to Event). Ids of the dEvent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dFinancialPeriod.description: An organisation unit's reported or planned results for one period. It holds the income-statement lines (revenue, costOfRevenue, operatingExpense, depreciation, interestExpense, incomeTax), the cash line capitalExpenditure, and investment figures. Subtotals such as gross margin, EBITDA, EBIT, net income and free cash flow are derived from these lines and are never stored. The cost and revenue periods it includes show where its figures come from. Linked to its unit by dOrganizationUnitReportsFinancialPeriod. Use kind Actual on its amounts for reported results and Estimate for a plan.

capitalExpenditure.description: Capital spend in the period, a cash line that is not part of the income statement; it reaches the income statement later as depreciation. It includes the included cost periods whose costNature is Capex. Same currency as revenue.

costOfRevenue.description: The direct cost of what was sold in the period, e.g. claims incurred for an insurer. It includes the included cost periods whose costFunction is CostOfRevenue. Same currency as revenue.

depreciation.description: Depreciation charged in the period: the share of earlier Capex spread over the assets' useful life. A non-cash cost. Same currency as revenue.

incomeTax.description: Income tax charged in the period. Same currency as revenue.

interestExpense.description: Interest paid or accrued on debt in the period. Same currency as revenue.

investedAssets.description: The value of invested assets at the end of the period; set asOf to that date. Same currency as revenue.

investmentIncome.description: Income from invested assets in the period. Same currency as revenue.

operatingExpense.description: All other operating cost in the period, including revenueLinkedExpense and the included cost periods whose costFunction is SellingGeneralAdmin or ResearchDevelopment. Excludes depreciation. Same currency as revenue.

periodLength.description: The length of the period, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P1Y for a fiscal year, P3M for a quarter. Periods of the same organisation unit must not overlap.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period.

revenue.description: Revenue earned in the period, e.g. net earned premium for an insurer, with an ISO 4217 currency as unit. It includes the revenue periods the statement includes (dFinancialPeriodIncludesRevenuePeriod). Use kind Actual for reported results and Estimate for a plan.

revenueLinkedExpense.description: The part of operatingExpense that grows and shrinks with revenue, e.g. commission and premium tax. Same currency as revenue.

dFinancialPeriodIncludesCostPeriod.description: includes Cost Period (Financial Period Includes Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The cost period is recorded in this statement: its amount is already part of the statement's operatingExpense (Opex) or capitalExpenditure (Capex). A model must not add it again.

dFinancialPeriodIncludesRevenuePeriod.description: includes Revenue Period (Financial Period Includes Revenue Period). Ids of the dRevenuePeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The revenue period is recorded in this statement: its amount is already part of the statement's revenue. A model must not add it again.

dOrganizationUnitReportsFinancialPeriod_.description: is reported by Org Unit (Org Unit Reports Financial Period). Ids of the dOrganizationUnit elements; multiplicity 1.

dGoal.description: a Goal is a measurable scope that the organization wants to achieve. Can be hierarchically decomposed.

AssumptionType.description: The levels at which assumptions were made to reach the goal, e.g. Business, Technology. The assumptions themselves belong in the simulation scenario, not here.

Priority.description: How important the goal is compared with the others, as a percentage from 1 to 100.

Value_amount.description: The baseline: the level of the targeted KPI when the goal was set, e.g. 103.2 % for the combined ratio. Set asOf to that date. The unit equals the KPI's UnitOfMeasure.

Value_Goal.description: The change the goal aims for, from Value_amount, in the same unit. Negative means reduce, e.g. -6.2 % to take the combined ratio from 103.2 % to 97.0 %. The target level is Value_amount + Value_Goal; zero means hold the level. The deadline is the latest finishDate of the goal's objectives.

Value_Name.description: The name of what the goal changes, e.g. "Combined ratio". It should match the name of the KPI the goal targets.

dGoalAggregatesGoal.description: parent Goal (Goal Aggregates Goal). Ids of the dGoal elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dGoalAggregatesGoal_inverse.description: Child Goal (Goal Aggregates Goal). Ids of the dGoal elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dGoalhasObjective.description: Has Objective (Goal has Milestone). Ids of the dObjective elements; multiplicity 0..*. The objectives are the goal's milestones. The goal's deadline is the latest finishDate among them.

A Growth pack is a collection of Initiatives architected for consistency and aimed to be executed in the same period.

ipRangeType.description: What the range is used for: Pod (container pods), Service (cluster services) or subNetwork.

ability to Implement.description: How confident you are that the organisation can deliver the initiative, as a percentage from 1 to 100.

actualStartDate.description: The date work actually started. Absent means not started.

initiativeHealth.description: The health of the initiative as a traffic light, from DeepGreen (on track) to Red (in serious trouble).

kind.description: The type of initiative, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Transformation", "Compliance", "Run".

purpose.description: Why the initiative exists: the problem it solves or the outcome it delivers, in one sentence.

dObjectInstanceofModel.description: Has an Instance (Instance of Model). Ids of the dModelClass elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dObjectInstanceofView.description: Has an Instance (Instance of View). Ids of the dView elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dObjective.description: The Objective is a non material achievement, other than a Goal, the objective has no specific value to be measured. it's a time-bounded milestone for an organization used to demonstrate progress towards a goal.

Category.description: A free categorisation of the objective, following your own taxonomy.

finishDate.description: The date by which the objective must be reached. The goal's deadline is the latest finishDate among its objectives.

Owner.description: The person or role accountable for reaching the objective.

Source.description: Where the information about this objective came from, e.g. the strategic plan.

Value_Goal.description: The change from the goal's Value_amount to reach by finishDate, in the goal's unit, e.g. -3.0 % by the first milestone. Absent means only the last objective carries the goal's target.

dGoalhasObjective_inverse.description: is related to Goal (Goal has Milestone). Ids of the dGoal elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dOpinion.description: A view or judgment formed about a Topic. That is formulated in an explicit fashion. Captures explicit stakeholder judgments on a topic.

dAccord.description: is in accord with other Opinion (According Opinion). Ids of the dOpinion elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dAccord_inverse.description: is in accord with original Opinion (According Opinion). Ids of the dOpinion elements; multiplicity 1.

dDiscord.description: is in discord with other Opinion (Discording opinion). Ids of the dOpinion elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dDiscord_inverse.description: is in discord with Original Opinion (Discording opinion). Ids of the dOpinion elements; multiplicity 1.

dStakeholderHasOpinion_inverse.description: is expressed by Stakeholder (Stakeholder Has Opinion). Ids of the dStakeholder elements; multiplicity 1.

dOpinionInner.description:
Captures implicit stakeholder opinions related to a topic.
A Stakeholder’s opinion that is relevant for the topic but is not formulated explicitly.

dStakeholderHasInnerOpinion_inverse.description: is thinked by Stakeholder (Stakeholder Has Inner Opinion). Ids of the dStakeholder elements; multiplicity 1.

dOrganizationUnit.description: Defines organizational units responsible for roles, can be decomposed

HeadCount.description: The number of people working in the unit, with unit {person}. Can be derived by adding up the FTEs of the unit's roles. Absent means not counted.

dOrganizationUnitReportsFinancialPeriod.description: reports Financial Period (Org Unit Reports Financial Period). Ids of the dFinancialPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The organisation unit's reported or planned results for one period. Each financial period belongs to exactly one organisation unit; the periods of one unit do not overlap.

dOrgUnitHasStakeholders.description: has Stakeholder (Org Unit has Stakeholders). Ids of the dStakeholder elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleisAssociatedToOrganization_inverse.description: has Role (Role is Associated To Organization). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dPhysicalService.description: a technical implementation of a service that runs on physical or virtual infrastructure, providing specific functionalities, usually in the form of software applications, middleware, databases, or platforms. It is concerned with the deployment, operation, and management of the technology stack, ensuring that the service is available, performant, and reliable. Examples include web servers, APIs, databases, and network services.

Category.description: A free categorisation of the service, following your own taxonomy, e.g. "Database", "Messaging".

execution_mode.description: Whether callers wait for the result (synchronous) or not (asynchronous).

LastStandardReviewDate.description: When the service was last reviewed against the technology standards.

NextStandardReviewDate.description: When the service is next due for review against the technology standards.

Owner.description: The person or team responsible for running the service.

port.description: The network port the service listens on, e.g. 5432.

protocol.description: The protocol the service uses on that port, e.g. https, TCP, UDP.

RetireDate.description: The date the service is, or is planned to be, switched off. Absent means no retirement is planned.

Source.description: Where the information about this service came from, e.g. a CMDB export.

dApplicationExposesService_inverse.description: Exposes Phy Service (Application Exposes Ph. Service). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dPhysicalServiceImplementsBusinessServic.description: Implement Biz Service (Physical Serv. Implements Biz Serv.). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSecurityGroupHasPhysicalService_inverse.description: Asociated to Sec. group (Security Group Has Service). Ids of the dSecurityGroup elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dServiceRealizedByAPI_inverse.description: is realized By API (Service Realized By API). Ids of the dAPI elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dPrinciple.description: Defines qualitative statements guiding architecture intent.

Implications.description: What the principle means in practice: what people must do, or stop doing, to follow it.

Owner.description: The stakeholder who owns the principle and decides on exceptions.

PrincipleID.description: Unique identifier of the principle, e.g. PR-DATA-01.

PrincipleMeasurement.description: The KPI used to check whether the principle is followed. Absent means it is not measured.

Priority.description: The priority of the principle relative to the others, e.g. 1 for the highest, used when principles conflict.

Rationale.description: Why the principle is needed and the outcome it leads to.

Source.description: Where the principle came from, e.g. the architecture board minutes of a given date.

Statement.description: The principle itself, in one clear sentence, e.g. "Data is an asset".

Type.description: The domain of the principle: guiding, business, data, application, integration or technology.

dDecisionRefersToPrinciple_inverse.description: is referenced by Decision (Decision refers To Principle). Ids of the dDecision elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProduct.description: Encapsulates outputs produced by business processes.

Owner.description: The role accountable for the product.

Price.description: The list price of the product, with an ISO 4217 currency as unit, e.g. 1200 CAD per P1Y for an annual premium. Contracts can set their own tariff. Absent means not priced.

RetireDate.description: The date the product is, or is planned to be, withdrawn from sale. Absent means no withdrawal is planned.

Source.description: Where the information about this product came from, e.g. the product catalogue.

ContractRelatedProduct_inverse.description: is related to Contract (Contract is Related to Product). Ids of the dContract elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProductHasCostPeriod.description: has Cost Period (Product Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. A direct cost of the product in one period, e.g. hardware bought for resale. Shared costs, such as a cloud platform used by several products, stay with their owner (the application); allocating them to products is a simulation step.

dProductHasRevenuePeriod.description: has Revenue Period (Product Has Revenue Period). Ids of the dRevenuePeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The revenue the product earns in one period, e.g. hardware sales or net earned premium of a product line.

dProductIncludesProcess.description: Includes Process (Product Includes Process). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dProgram.description: A group of Growth Packages that achieve a complex outcome for the organization

dProgramHasBudgetPeriod.description: has Budget Period (Program Has Budget Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The spending cap for all initiatives in the program (through its growth packages) in one period. The budget periods of one program do not overlap.

dProgramIsOrganizedInPackages.description: is organized In Packages (Program is organized In Packages). Ids of the dGrowthPackage elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dPublicCluster.description: A public cloud-based cluster, following the ArchiMate concept of Infrastructure Service provided by external cloud providers (Google, AWS, etc.).

configFile.description: The name of the configuration file used to create or connect to the cluster, e.g. config_google.conf.

NodeNum.description: The number of nodes in the cluster, e.g. 3.

provider.description: The cloud provider that runs the cluster, e.g. AWS, Azure, Google.

amount.description: The numeric value, as a decimal, e.g. 0.02. Its meaning is given by unit, per and basis.

asOf.description: The date the value refers to, e.g. the date of a measurement or the end of a period. Absent means not dated.

basis.description: What amount is counted for, when it is a ratio to something other than time, e.g. "per FTE", "per claim". Absent means no such denominator.

kind.description: How the value was obtained: Actual (measured or reported), Estimate (planned or forecast) or Assumption (assumed for a scenario). Absent means not known; unspecified says the same and is kept for older models.

per.description: The time period amount refers to, as an xsd:duration, for rates and periodic costs: P stands for period and T marks the time part, e.g. PT30M (30 minutes), P1D (1 day), P1M (1 month), P1Y (1 year). Absent means amount is not a rate.

unit.description: The unit of amount: an ISO 4217 currency code for money, e.g. CAD, otherwise a UCUM code, e.g. %, h, {FTE}, {claim}.

dQuantityValue.description: Represents a measurable value expressed as a numeric amount and a unit of measurement. It provides a reusable structure for quantitative properties of DAF elements.

dRegion.description: A geographic area containing clusters and zones, aligned with ArchiMate's Location concept for representing deployment geography.

dRegionAggregatesCluster.description: Aggregates Cluster (Region Aggregates Cluster). Ids of the dCluster elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dZoneAggregatesRegion_inverse.description: is Aggregated in Zone (Zone Aggregates Region). Ids of the dZone elements; multiplicity 1.

dRequirement.description:
A Business guide line about the Enterprise or the project. Requirements can be decomposed. A requirement is formulated in a SMART fashion and uses Moscow verbs (Must Have, Should Have, Could Have, and Would Like to Have.).
  • Must Have: These are the requirements that are considered essential for the success of the initiative and must be meet for the system to function. They are often referred to as "hard" or "mandatory". requirements and are typically expressed in Boolean format as "true" or "1".
  • Should Have: These are the requirements that are considered important, but not essential. They are typically expressed in Boolean format as "maybe" or "0/1" and are often used to prioritize the development of the system.
  • Could Have: These are the requirements that are considered desirable but not essential. They are typically expressed in Boolean format as "false" or "0". They are used to identify potential enhancements to the system that can be added at a later date.
  • Would Like to Have: These are the requirements that are considered less important and are often used to identify potential future enhancements to the system.
In addition, the requirement should be SMART, which stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. SMART requirements are clear, concise, and easy to understand, and they provide a clear way to measure the success of the project.

Author.description: Who wrote the requirement: name and role in the project, e.g. "Ana Diaz, Analyst".

Priority.description: The priority of the requirement as a percentage from 1 to 100. Requirements are ordered by it.

Proofreader.description: Who confirmed the requirement: name and role in the project, e.g. "Tom Lee, Client". Every requirement needs one.

Status.description: Where the requirement is in the workflow, e.g. Proposed, Validated, Mandatory.

Type.description: The kind of requirement, e.g. Business Rule, Security, Performance, Scalability.

dIssueStopsRealizationOfRequirement_inve.description: is stopped by Issue (Issue Stops Realization Of Req). Ids of the dIssue elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRequirementContainsRequirement.description: is contained by Requirement (Requirement Contains Req). Ids of the dRequirement elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRequirementContainsRequirement_inverse.description: Contains Requirement (Requirement Contains Req). Ids of the dRequirement elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dRequirementIsRelatedToGoal.description: specifies Goal (req related to Goal). Ids of the dGoal elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRequirementIsSatisfiedByFeature_inverse.description: is realized by Feature (is Satisfied By). Ids of the dFeature elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dResource.description: a type of Asset supporting a Business capability

# of items.description: How many units of the resource are available, e.g. 40 for 40 vehicles.

depreciationMethod.description: How its Capex is spread over usefulLife: StraightLine or DecliningBalance. The depreciation schedule is derived from the Capex cost periods, inServiceDate, usefulLife and this method; it is not stored.

inServiceDate.description: The date the asset went into use; depreciation starts here. Absent means not recorded.

usefulLife.description: How long the asset is depreciated over, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P5Y. Absent means the asset is not capitalised or the life is not recorded.

dResourceHasCostPeriod.description: has Cost Period (Resource Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The cost of the resource in one period: its purchase (Capex) or its upkeep, e.g. maintenance of an owned fleet (Opex).

dResourceimpactedByRisk_inverse.description: is impacted by Risk (Resource impacted by Risk). Ids of the dRisk elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dResourceSupportsCapability.description: Supports Capability (Resource supports Capability). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 1..*.

dRevenuePeriod.description: Revenue earned by one product or contract in one period, reported (kind Actual) or planned (kind Estimate). It can be included in the financial period of the organisation unit whose books it lands in (dFinancialPeriodIncludesRevenuePeriod).

amount.description: The revenue earned in the period, with an ISO 4217 currency as unit. Use kind Actual for reported revenue and Estimate for a plan.

periodLength.description: The length of the period, as an xsd:duration, e.g. P1M, P1Y. The revenue periods of one product or contract must not overlap.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period.

dContractHasRevenuePeriod_inverse.description: is revenue of Contract (Contract Has Revenue Period). Ids of the dContract elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dFinancialPeriodIncludesRevenuePeriod_in.description: is included in Financial Period (Financial Period Includes Revenue Period). Ids of the dFinancialPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dProductHasRevenuePeriod_inverse.description: is revenue of Product (Product Has Revenue Period). Ids of the dProduct elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dRisk.description: a risk Identifies and assesses potential issue impacting other elements. It is a potential future Issue. Can be hierarchically decomposed.

likelihood.description: The probability that the risk becomes an issue, on a scale of 1 (very unlikely) to 100 (almost certain). Absent means not assessed.

RiskStrategy.description: How the risk is handled: Terminate (remove the cause), Treat (reduce it), Tolerate (accept it) or Transfer (e.g. insure or outsource it).

Severity.description: The impact if the risk happens, on a scale of 1 (negligible) to 100 (critical). Absent means not assessed.

dApplicationRisk.description: is related to Application (Application Risk). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dResourceimpactedByRisk.description: impact Resouce (Resource impacted by Risk). Ids of the dResource elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRiskIsRelatedToRisk.description: target Risk (Risk is related to Risk). Ids of the dRisk elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRiskIsRelatedToRisk_inverse.description: Source Risk (Risk is related to Risk). Ids of the dRisk elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRiskRealizedByIssue_inverse.description: is realized by Issue (realized by Issue). Ids of the dIssue elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dRole.description: The usual or expected function of an actor, or the part somebody or something plays in a particular action or event. An actor may have a number of roles.

CostRate.description: The cost of one unit of the role's capacity, e.g. 85000 CAD per P1Y with basis "per FTE". It is a rate, not spend: the spend on the role goes into its cost periods (dRoleHasCostPeriod). Absent means not known.

DegreeOfUtilisation.description: The share of the role's capacity that is in use, with unit %, e.g. 88 %. Absent means not measured.

FTEs.description: The number of full-time equivalents working in the role, with unit {FTE}, e.g. 42 {FTE}. Absent means not counted.

isSkillsAvailable.description: true when the people in the role have the skills it needs; otherwise false.

isSkillsDefined.description: true when the skills the role needs are written down; otherwise false.

Owner.description: The person or unit accountable for the role, e.g. its line manager.

Source.description: Where the information about this role came from, e.g. the HR system.

User.description: A free categorisation of the role, following your own taxonomy.

dRoleConsumesService.description: Consumes Service (Role Consumes Service). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*. The role uses the service's output; it does not do the service's work. Use dRoleStaffsService for the roles whose capacity delivers the service.

dRoleExecutesCapability_inverse.description: executes Capability (role Executes Capability). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleHasCostPeriod.description: has Cost Period (Role Has Cost Period). Ids of the dCostPeriod elements; multiplicity 0..*. The spend on the role in one period, e.g. salaries of its FTEs. The rate per FTE is CostRate.

dRoleHasSkill.description: has SKill (Role has skill). Ids of the dSkill elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleisAssociatedToOrganization.description: works in Organization (Role is Associated To Organization). Ids of the dOrganizationUnit elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dRoleIsPerformedByActor_inverse.description: is executed by Actor (Role isPerformed By Actor). Ids of the dActor elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleMaintainsApplication.description: maintains Application (Role Maintains Application). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dRoleStaffsService.description: staffs Service (Role Staffs Service). Ids of the dBusinessService elements; multiplicity 0..*. The role's capacity delivers the service: it does the service's work.

dRule.description: A precise business condition or constraint, implemented at a specific point in an application. Modeled as an operation with package visibility on a dController, which acts as the rule set. Its Statement is the human-readable rule passed to an LLM to generate the implementation.

Certainty.description: Explicit when modeled directly; Inferred when extracted from legacy code.

RuleKind.description: The OMG category of the rule: Production, Integrity, Derivation or Reaction.

SourceEvidence.description: Where the rule was found in legacy code: program, paragraph or section, and line range, e.g. "LGICUS01 / 2000-VALIDATE-AGE / L412-L431".

Statement.description: Human-readable statement of the rule, precise enough to pass to an LLM for implementation, e.g. "Ensure Customer.Age >= 18 before Account.Creation".

dSecurityGroup.description: Controls and manages access and permissions between services, in line with TOGAF's Security Architecture for protecting digital assets.

dNetworkHasSecurityGroup_inverse.description: is associated to Network (Network Has Security Group). Ids of the dNetwork elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSecurityGroupHasPhysicalService.description: has Physical Service (Security Group Has Service). Ids of the dPhysicalService elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSkill.description: an ability that some role possesses with various degree

SkillCategory.description: The group the skill belongs to, e.g. "Technical", "Domain", "Leadership".

SkillLevel.description: How well the skill is mastered, on your own scale, e.g. Basic, Proficient, Expert.

dRoleHasSkill_inverse.description: known by Role (Role has skill). Ids of the dRole elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dStakeholder.description: Represents any party or force influencing the domain of interest. Any person or force that have an interest in the considered domain. This is typically indicated by name, can be connected with a Role in the organization. A stakeholder has open and Inner opinions that are relevant for the subject matter.

Attitude.description: How favourable the stakeholder is to the change: Low (opposed), Medium (neutral) or High (supportive).

Knowledge.description: How much the stakeholder knows about the subject: Low, Medium or High.

Legitimacy.description: How widely the stakeholder's claim is accepted as appropriate by others: Low, Medium or High.

Power.description: How far the stakeholder can impose their will on the outcome: Low, Medium or High.

RACI.description: The stakeholder's responsibility: R (Responsible: does the work), A (Accountable: answers for the result; only one per task), C (Consulted: gives input before the work is done) or I (Informed: is told the outcome).

role.description: The role the stakeholder plays in the organisation, when it is in the model.

Urgency.description: How much the stakeholder's concerns call for immediate attention: Low, Medium or High.

dApplicationHasOwner_inverse.description: has Owner (Application has Owner). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dOrgUnitHasStakeholders_inverse.description: is concerned with Organization (Org Unit has Stakeholders). Ids of the dOrganizationUnit elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dStakeholderHasInnerOpinion.description: Has Inner Opinion (Stakeholder Has Inner Opinion). Ids of the dOpinionInner elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dStakeholderHasOpinion.description: Has Opinion (Stakeholder Has Opinion). Ids of the dOpinion elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSubNetwork.description: A subset of a network, used to organize and isolate portions of the network. Equivalent to an ArchiMate Node, responsible for networking resources.

dNetworkAggregatesSubNetwork_inverse.description: is Aggregated in Network (Network Aggregates SubNetwork). Ids of the dNetwork elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSubNetworkAggregatesIPRange.description: Aggregates IP Range (SubNetwork Aggregates IP Range). Ids of the dIPRange elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dSystem.description:
A system configuration. Settings are modeled as attributes with default values, each attribute of the System Config becomes a line in the configuration file.
e.g. SystemConfig .path = c:/users/app

config.description: The configuration file the settings are written to, e.g. config.ini.

platform.description: The platform the settings apply to, e.g. "production", "Windows".

dApplicationconfiguredbySystemConfigurat.description: configures Application (Application configured by System Configuration). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dTable.description: Represents physical tables in a database schema.

Database.description: The database schema that holds the table, e.g. claims.

dTableProvidesPersistenceForModelClass_i.description: Provides Persistence For Model (Table Provides Persistence to Model). Ids of the dModelClass elements; multiplicity 1.

dTest.description: Represents a mechanism for verifying or validating the functionality, behavior, or compliance of am application component . Tests can include automated or manual procedures designed to ensure alignment with requirements, detect defects, and confirm expected outcomes.

dTest_ApplicationComponent.description: Test validates Component (Test validates Component). Ids of the dApplicationComponent elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dUserStory.description: Captures user-centric requirements expressed as stories.

EstimatedEffort.description: The estimated effort to deliver the story, in hours, e.g. 8.

StoryDetails.description: The story itself: "As a <role> I want <scope> so that <value>".

TestScenario.description: How to check that the story is done: the situation and the expected result, e.g. "Given ... when ... then ...".

dUseCaseHasStory.description: Is associated to Use Case (Use Case Has Story). Ids of the dBusinessUseCase elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dValue.description: An attribute of a Node value type used in DAF. These values are persistent

app_data_type.description: How the value is handled by the application: DATATYPE_ATTRIBUTE, DATATYPE_ELEMENT, DATATYPE_DONTCARE or DATATYPE_IGNORE.

column_name.description: The name of the database column. Empty means the value's name is used.

db_data_type.description: The column type in the database, e.g. VARCHAR(255), INT, DATE.

display_type.description: How the value is shown, e.g. text, image.

input_type.description: The HTML input control used to edit the value, e.g. text, or select#fix:key1[val1]|key2[val2] for a fixed list.

is_editable.description: true when users can change the value; otherwise false.

restrictions_description.description: The message shown to users when the value breaks a restriction, e.g. "Enter a date as DD.MM.YYYY".

restrictions_match.description: A regular expression the value must match, e.g. [0-3][0-9]\.[0-1][0-9]\.[0-9]{4} for a date.

restrictions_not_match.description: A regular expression the value must not match.

dValueRef.description: A Node value type used in DAF that reference another Node Value, similar to a foreign Key. These values are persistent

reference_value.description: The dValue this reference points to, like a foreign key.

dValueStream.description:
A representation of  an end-to end collection  of value-adding  Business Processes that create an overall result for a customer, stakeholder or end user. 
A sequence of activities an enterprise undertakes to deliver on a customer request. More broadly, the sequence of activities required to design, produce, and deliver a good or service to a customer, and it includes the dual flows of information and material.

Criticality.description: How much the value stream matters to the customer and the business, from Negligible Impact to Significant Impact. Leave Not Analyzed until it is assessed.

entrance criteria.description: What starts the value stream, e.g. "customer requests a quote".

exit criteria.description: What ends the value stream, i.e. the value delivered, e.g. "policy issued and paid".

is Decomposed.description: true when the value stream has been broken down into stages; otherwise false.

dValueStreamEnablesCapability.description: Enables Capability (Value Stream Enables Capability). Ids of the dCapability elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dValueStreamIncludesProcesses.description: Includes Process (Value Stream Includes Processes). Ids of the dBusinessProcess elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dView.description: A View used in DAF. Controller, Views and Associations define the application flow

dControllerGovernsView_inverse.description: is Governed by Controller (Governs View). Ids of the dController elements; multiplicity 0..1.

dObjectInstanceofView_inverse.description: Istance of View (Instance of View). Ids of the dObject elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dVolume.description: Refers to the storage assigned to containers, ensuring persistence, aligning with the Data Object in ArchiMate’s Application Layer.

MountPath.description: The path inside the container where the volume is mounted, e.g. /var/lib/postgresql/data.

name.description: The name of the volume, e.g. claims-data.

subPath.description: A sub-directory of the volume to mount instead of its root. Empty means the whole volume.

dContainerAggregatesVolume_inverse.description: is Aggregated in Container (Container Aggregates Volume). Ids of the dContainer elements; multiplicity 0..*.

dZone.description: Defines macro divisions containing regions mapped to ArchiMate’s Infrastructure Service.

dZoneAggregatesRegion.description: Aggregates Region (Zone Aggregates Region). Ids of the dRegion elements; multiplicity 0..*.
